name: BodyMap
founded: 1982, London, from a Camden Market stall. Liquidation reported 1986; B-basic lingered into the early 90s.
founders: Stevie Stewart + David Holah (both Middlesex Polytechnic, 1979–82). Women-co-founded: yes. Not women-only — say the partnership clearly.
women_founded: Women-co-founded: yes. Partnership with David Holah — say so.
story: They met day one at Middlesex. Graduation collection bought by Browns. The name comes from artist Enrico Job, who photographed every part of his body and collaged a flat “body map” — they cut patterns the same way, holes in unexpected places, flesh as part of the garment.

Collection titles were feral: Barbie Takes a Trip, Querelle Meets Olive Oil, The Cat in the Hat Takes a Rumble with the Techno Fish. They rebranded lycra as high fashion, dressed Michael Clark’s dancers, and were the house look of 80s London clubland. After a New York “New London” show produced with Susanne Bartsch they were stars overnight, then the business imploded.
style_codes: Stretched jersey, holes, layered knits, wild prints, unisex club shapes
